children: Major Japanese food manufacturer House Foods Group Inc. on Monday revealed that it is considering selling Ichibanya Co., operator of the Curry House CoCo Ichibanya restaurant chain.
With the move, House Foods aims to focus resources on growth areas amid a harsher business environment caused by rising prices and other factors.
House Foods and Ichibanya released statements saying they are considering every possible option, including the delisting of Ichibanya from the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

Since Ichibanya's establishment in 1978, its curry roux has been supplied by House Foods. The food manufacturer acquired a stake in Ichibanya in 1998. In 2015, it invested about 30 billion yen to raise its stake from 19.5% to 51%, turning Ichibanya into a consolidated subsidiary. The two companies have cooperated on areas such as ingredient procurement and overseas expansion.

Ichibanya recorded consolidated sales of 65.5 billion yen in the fiscal year ending February 2026, up 7.4% from the previous fiscal year, while net profit dropped by 19.2% to 2.5 billion yen. As of Feb. 28, the company operated 1,285 stores in Japan and 218 stores overseas, including non-curry restaurants.

House Foods and Ichibanya are both listed on the TSE's Prime Market. It is believed that House Foods also intends to resolve the parent-subsidiary listing — a practice that faces long-standing criticism because the parent company's intentions as a major shareholder are easily reflected in the subsidiary's management, potentially harming the subsidiary's general shareholders.
